target: Lithuania, couple where both adults are age 25-30 and both work

evidence.fact: OECD EU-SILC 2024 living-arrangement data show Lithuania's 20-29 population split among parental home, living alone, partnered and other household types; partnership share rises materially with age within this band.
evidence.source: OECD Affordable Housing Database HM1.4, updated 2025-10-02

evidence.fact: Eurostat 2024 housing-conditions chart shows only about one quarter of Lithuania's 25-29-year-olds still linked to the parental household, much lower than for 20-24.
evidence.source: Eurostat, Young people - housing conditions, ilc_lvps08

evidence.fact: Lithuanian first-marriage ages are around the late twenties / early thirties, supporting a materially higher partnership share for 25-30 than for 20-24.
evidence.source: Official Statistics Portal / VDA marriage statistics

evidence.fact: Eurostat EU-LFS 2024 Lithuania age profile shows high employment by ages 25-30, but no direct public cross-tab 'both partners work × both age 25-30'.
evidence.source: Eurostat ad hoc EU-LFS extraction, Participation of young people in education and the labour market

safeguards: Do not call this an official count.
Do not use 515 / denominator as programme take-up: numerator covers legally defined young families up to age 36, denominator is 25-30 working couples.
Use rounded range publicly; avoid fake precision.
Replace with direct official microdata/cross-tab if later available.
